plain_text:
W hile a cold, flu, or COVID-19 can strike at any time,
you're more likely to pick up a virus in the winter
than other times of the year. The cold, dry air in the
winter months provides perfect conditions for viruses to spread.
People are also more likely to gather indoors to avoid the cold
weather, making it easier for viruses to spread in large numbers.

plain_text:
The best way to protect yourself from a virus is to get vaccinated if
one is available. But even if you're vaccinated, you should take the
following steps to avoid getting sick:
semantic_text: The best way to protect yourself from a virus is to get vaccinated if one is available. But even if you're vaccinated, you should take the following steps to avoid getting sick:

plain_text:
■ Mask up. Wear a mask in crowded and other public areas
where viruses can spread quickly.
■ Wash your hands frequently. Washing with soap and warm
water is still the best way to keep clean, but hand sanitizer is
good in a pinch. Just because you don't see any dirt or grime
on your hands, that doesn't mean germs aren't there!
■ Disinfect surfaces. To make sure you're reducing germs,
consider using disinfectants like bleach or antibacterial wipes
when cleaning surfaces. Some high-touch surfaces to focus on
include counters, doorknobs, faucets and toilet handles, light
switches, remotes, phones, and toys.
■ Avoid close contact with people who are sick. If someone
you're living with comes down with a virus, try to stay in
different rooms as much as possible, use separate dishware, and
wipe down shared spaces such as bathrooms. If you must be in
the same room, try to keep some distance between one another.

Some high-touch surfaces to focus on include counters, doorknobs, faucets and toilet handles, light switches, remotes, phones, and toys. ■ Avoid close contact with people who are sick. If someone you're living with comes down with a virus, try to stay in different rooms as much as possible, use separate dishware, and wipe down shared spaces such as bathrooms. If you must be in the same room, try to keep some distance between one another.

plain_text:
Access to fresh air also lowers the risk of infection. Air purifiers
are great if you have one, and if the weather's warm enough,
a cracked window can help fresh air flow into the room.
semantic_text: Access to fresh air also lowers the risk of infection. Air purifiers are great if you have one, and if the weather's warm enough, a cracked window can help fresh air flow into the room.

plain_text:
■ Try not to touch your eyes, nose, and mouth . Though
COVID-19 mainly spreads through the air, many other viruses
spread when someone touches a surface with the virus on it and
then touches their eyes, nose, or mouth. This can help a virus
enter the body.
semantic_text: ■ Try not to touch your eyes, nose, and mouth . Though COVID-19 mainly spreads through the air, many other viruses spread when someone touches a surface with the virus on it and then touches their eyes, nose, or mouth. This can help a virus enter the body.

plain_text:
■ Avoid close contact with people, including the ones you live
with, as much as possible.
■ Get tested—knowing what's causing the infection can help
inform treatment decisions. Older individuals and those with
existing medical conditions should call their doctor if they test
positive for COVID-19.
semantic_text: ■ Avoid close contact with people, including the ones you live with, as much as possible. ■ Get tested—knowing what's causing the infection can help inform treatment decisions. Older individuals and those with existing medical conditions should call their doctor if they test positive for COVID-19.

plain_text:
If you have a virus, be sure to stay away from others (especially if you're
not wearing a mask).
semantic_text: If you have a virus, be sure to stay away from others (especially if you're not wearing a mask).
